questions.question: What belongs in head versus body, and how many of each can a document have?
questions.answer: head holds metadata: title, charset, viewport, description, stylesheet and script links, base. body holds all visible content. A valid document has exactly one head and one body inside the html root.

questions.question: Why must meta charset appear early in the head?
questions.answer: The browser needs the encoding before it decodes the rest of the bytes. Charset must be declared within the first 1024 bytes, otherwise characters such as ₹ or é may render as mojibake.

questions.question: What does the viewport meta tag do, and which values hurt accessibility?
questions.answer: It tells mobile browsers to use the device width and initial scale instead of a virtual desktop width. user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1 block pinch-zoom and should be avoided.

questions.question: List four link rel values and what each does.
questions.answer: stylesheet loads CSS, icon sets the favicon, canonical names the preferred URL for SEO, and preload fetches a critical resource early. Other examples include alternate and manifest.

questions.question: Write a head for Kakade's blog with UTF-8, responsive viewport, title, description, canonical URL, and stylesheet.
questions.answer:
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
  <title>Kakade — HTML Notes</title>
  <meta name="description" content="Beginner-friendly HTML interview notes." />
  <link rel="canonical" href="https://kakade.dev/html" />
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/style.css" />
</head>

questions.question: Use base to make every relative link on Kakade's page resolve to https://kakade.dev/.
A page shows â‚¹499 instead of ₹499. What is the most likely cause?
questions.answer: A missing or late meta charset declaration, so the browser decoded UTF-8 bytes with a legacy encoding. Add <meta charset="UTF-8" /> as the first element in head and save the file as UTF-8.

questions.question: Why is <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, user-scalable=no"> a problem?
questions.answer: It disables pinch-zoom, which prevents low-vision users from enlarging content and fails WCAG expectations. Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and let users zoom.
